item.title: WARDOGS: Best Recon Sniper Loadout
item.description:
WARDOGS rewards patience, especially if you're in the mood to take on the role of a recon sniper. Recons aren't supposed to chase the Hot Zone; instead, they should focus on a safe camping spot with good sights on the battlefield, but tactics can only get you so far. Below, we'll share the best recon loadout in WARDOGS so you can master the scope and provide essential cover and distance shooting for your team.

10 Best Military Open-World Games, Ranked

Whether part of the military or going against it, these are the best open-world games for armed combat.

2
By John Cunningham

Best Low-Level Sniper Loadout in WARDOGS

Unlocked by Recon Level 7

  • Primary Weapon: SKS Marksman Rifle
  • Attachments:
    • DTK-1 Brake Muzzle
    • SKS Bipod
    • 6x Precision Rifle Scope

  • Sidearm: GGX 17
  • Specialist Slot: Small Hammer
  • Gear:
    • Helmet
    • Armor
    • Vest
    • Scout Backpack

  • Items in Backpack:
    • Bandage x10
    • Building Supplies x1
    • 7.62 Standard Ammo (FMJ) x120
    • GGX 17 RND Magazine x1

The SKS is a reliable marksman rifle for sniping, with a good fire rate and a 10-bullet capacity. The weapon's recoil is lower than dedicated sniper rifles, making it easier to land consecutive shots, but bipods make it even smoother and easier to control. The brake muzzle will also help with the vertical recoil. If you deploy the bipods, this build will give you an almost recoil-free sniping experience.

While the SKS cannot one-shot armored enemies, landing two shots in quick succession isn't difficult with the build above. One last benefit of the SKS is that when you are caught in a close-range or mid-range gunfight, you can remove the scope and have a reliable marksman rifle that can turn the tide in your favor .

For the specialist slot, I prefer a small hammer over monoculars or a Rangefinder. The small hammer will help you fortify your sniping position and prevent enemies from rushing you so easily, especially if you are on top of a tower.

Best Mid-Level Sniper Loadout in WARDOGS

Unlocked by Recon Level 21

  • Primary Weapon: SV98 Sniper Rifle
  • Attachments:
    • SRVV Brake Muzzle
    • SV98 Bipods
    • 6x to 10x Scope Mrad

  • Sidearm: GGX 17
  • Specialist Slot: Small Hammer
  • Gear:
    • Helmet
    • Armor
    • Vest
    • Field Backpack

  • Items in Backpack:
    • Bandage x10
    • Building Supplies x1
    • 7.62x54mm Standard Ammo (FMJ) x80
    • SV98 10 RND Magazine x2
    • GGX 17 RND Magazine x1

If you are looking for a meaningful level in your sniping experience, the SV98 is the next best thing to try. The weapon is a dedicated sniper rifle with very high vertical recoil. Although the attachments above will reduce the recoil significantly, it's still difficult to land two back-to-back shots on a single target, and for most fights, you won't need more than one shot.

The SV98 can one-shot armorless targets as well as those wearing low-level armor . So, as long as you hit a headshot or a torso shot, the kill is guaranteed. This is a massive compensation for the insane vertical recoil.

The downside of the SV98 is that it uses a magazine, and each magazine takes up two spaces in your backpack. Although it makes reloading faster, when all your magazines are empty, you need to take a lengthy break to fill them.

Unlike the SKS, you cannot count on the SV98 for close-range or mid-range gunfights, and that's when the sidearm and small hammer become even more important, because you don't want to leave your nest anytime soon.

We'll have a high level loadout soon, but for now, stick with the medium level one!

Zeroing in WARDOGS, Explained

Regardless of the build you choose, zeroing is a crucial part of sniping. Your weapon should always be ready for the distance you are looking at; otherwise, your aim won't be accurate.

An easy way to measure the distance is to switch the zeroing distances one by one while shooting at a concrete object at the same distance that you are looking at. Whenever you see the point of impact is closest to the center dot of your scope, that's the most accurate range for your weapon .

You can also check your zeroing based on your distance from the Hot Zone, assuming you are not inside the Hot Zone. Just ping the point you are looking at, and then check its location on the map. Now, compare your distance to the target point with your distance from the Hot Zone, and you can have a good guess at the distance.

Of course, these methods are for situations where you don't have the Range Finder device unlocked, or you don't want to use it for any reason. Otherwise, Range Finder is the best tool that you can use for zeroing your weapon.

WARDOGS Sniper/Recon Tips & Best Spots

Wardogs features an expansive map, but almost all gunfights happen inside the Control Zone. There is no better spot for a sniper than elevated structures or hills. The Control Zone always features a bunch of towers, and it's highly recommended for each faction to capture the closest tower to their HQ as soon as possible.

Towers are super important in Wardogs because they are the tallest structures and highest points in the Control Zone . Not only can you overlook a big part of the Control Zone, but you will also have a direct line of fire on other towers, which turns it into a battle between snipers. And that's the risky part of controlling a tower.

Another risk is when your tower is getting raided. A sniper has significant control over the surroundings of the tower, but when numerous enemies manage to reach the foot of the tower, there is not much a sniper can do. That's why setting up the tower's surroundings with the correct set of defensive structures is highly recommended .

One of the best things you can do to delay an enemy from rushing into a tower is to use barbed wire to create a specific path into the tower. You can see an example of this in the image below.

This route makes sure that there is only one entry path to the tower stairs. Enemies cannot rush from multiple sides, and when they enter the path, they have a predictable movement pattern. This is mostly helpful for other players on the ground who try to hold the site, including the tower.

Now, let's focus on your own positioning inside or on top of the tower. It's quite important to find a position with a one-way sight line . You don't want to expose yourself to multiple directions. That's why leaning while peeking as a sniper is quite important. If you are inside the tower and try to peek from the wide windows, move to the side of the window that has a sturdy wall with no openings, and then try to peek from the corner of the window by leaning.

If you are on the roof of the tower, it's hard to maintain such a position. That's why you should usually use the rooftop only to target people on other towers . Still, you can find a position behind the hut on the roof that let's have visuals only on one tower, while your back is only exposed to your faction's HQ side.

The church on the Bakurani map is also a good spot for sniping . If you get inside the church and peek from one of its side doors, that will provide a good view over the surrounding area, especially knowing that the church is located on top of a hill. That said, you definitely need to put some barbed wire on other church entrances to avoid any flanking. Do this only when there are not many teammates around you.

When there are enough players from your faction around the church, you can upgrade your positioning by building a Recon Tent on the tip of the hill, outside the church, and crawling inside it. This will give you an even better spot to get kills.

Another good spot for a sniper is the entry points into the Control Zone from other factions' sides . The factions usually come in from the west, south, and east of the Control Zone. So, camping at any of these entry points that is closer to one of the rival factions will give you a great spot to kill the opponent. This is a huge element of surprise, because when players are near their own tower, they usually move recklessly.

However, this will risk your life too. If there are buildings near the entry points, peeking from the windows of a building would be ideal, but you need to change your building repeatedly to avoid dead players respawning and raiding your position.

Sitting in open spaces is not recommended unless you are near your faction's entry point to the Control Zone . It's easy to get flanked inside the Control Zone, and snipers are the most vulnerable soldiers to flanking.

We spoke about places that you should be as a sniper, but there are also places that you need to avoid. The Hot Zone is by far the worst place a sniper can be. Unless you are hiding in a good sniping spot and the Hot Zone comes towards you, there is no reason for a sniper to be in the Hot Zone. However, spots that overlook the Hot Zone are highly recommended.

Another thing that you shouldn't do is move constantly . Aside from the tiny sniper glare, the only thing that can give away your position is moving. Staying stationary is key to successful camouflage. As long as you don't move, it's quite difficult for other players and even snipers to distinguish you from the terrain. But as soon as you move, you can become an easy target.

That's why using a Recon Tent is recommended, especially when you are sniping from hills or among the trees. Recon Tent forces you to get prone, limits your sudden movements, and creates an extra layer of camouflage.

WARDOGS

item.title: 5 Open-World RPGs That Were Perfect From Day One
item.description:
Nowadays, so many massive AAA games launch with missing or broken pieces that aren't fixed until after release, if at all. Considering their sheer size, open-world RPGs rarely arrive in top shape, and many folks nowadays prefer to wait a few months (or years) before picking up these games. By then, they should be in peak form... and finally match what a handful of titles achieved on Day One.

Even all-time great open-world RPGs like The Witcher 3 had less-than-smooth debuts, even if the positives largely outweighed the negatives. Frankly, nobody should have to wait weeks or months to play the "best" version of a game they bought, let alone a functioning one. Perfect open-world RPGs are very rare, and ones that launched like that are almost non-existent. These games accomplished the impossible.

"Perfect" is a bit hyperbolic, but these open-world RPGs were in tip-top shape from the start , and Day One players didn't have to live through any growing pains. They may have improved after launch, but they started from a very strong position.

I'm letting some technical issues slide , as open-world RPGs have so many moving parts that something will almost certainly break. These games delivered on their promises on Day One .

Also, no action-adventure games like Breath of the Wild or Ghost of Tsushima ​​​​​.

Elden Ring Was A Souls Masterpiece From The Very Start

A Day One Phenomenon

  • The PC version launched with quite a few issues, and the frame rate could have been more consistent on consoles.

Elden Ring didn't launch with a roadmap, microtransactions, or promises of upcoming patches; no, it simply arrived, fully formed and ready to play .

By early 2022, the open-world genre was reaching its lowest point, as it had devolved into exhausting checklists and time-wasters. When FromSoftware revealed plans to transplant the Souls formula into an open world, reception was initially mixed, as some folks feared the developer's trademark tight level design would not survive.

6 Hardest Japanese Open-World RPGs, Ranked

While not impossible to beat, these RPGs are some of the hardest games in their genre. The fact that they're open-world just amplifies the difficulty

4
By Tristan Jurkovich

Well, those fears disappeared the second somebody booted Elden Ring and stepped out of the Stranded Graveyard into Limgrave, only to immediately meet their end at the hands of the Tree Sentinel. Brutal in difficulty and tone, the Lands Between instantly became the gaming world's new home, and Day One players found themselves collectively exploring a hellscape packed with secrets, horrors, bosses, weapons, and fashion.

I played Elden Ring on PC, so my experience had its share of technical hiccups... but the game and its design philosophy were pretty much perfect from the first second . The content's sheer density was, and still is, impressive, as you can go in any direction and find something worthwhile almost instantly. All of this was done through natural exploration and without relying on map icons; I cannot describe the joy of realizing that a simple elevator ride can lead to a subterranean civilization rather than a small dungeon.

Xenoblade Chronicles Was Perfect When It Finally Arrived

Pushing The Nintendo Wii To Its Absolute Limit

  • North Americans had to beg Nintendo to bring the game over.

OK, this one is a bit of a special case, and it has nothing to do with the game's actual quality. Famously, Nintendo didn't seem interested in releasing Xenoblade Chronicles in North America, prompting fans to stage the "Operation Rainfall" campaign to finally set things right. You could argue this nonsense disqualifies XC from a perfect launch, since millions of people didn't get to play it on Day One; however, the outcry was so loud because the game was so fantastic.

The Nintendo Wii was incredibly underpowered for its era, barely offering more juice than a GameCube. An expansive open-world RPG should not have worked on this console, but Monolith Soft not only succeeded in performing a technical miracle, but also a mechanical one . Besides somehow avoiding mid-zone loading screens in its major open areas, Xenoblade Chronicles tells an ambitious story set in a world found on the body of two warring titans, and you can actually see them in real-time.

Monolith introduced a real-time battle system that layered mechanics on top of each other, keeping it interesting for 50+ hours. The world and its enemies didn't feel static, and XC included quality-of-life adjustments that were ahead of the curve at the time. For an open-world RPG created on the Wii, XC was an uncompromised masterclass in scale and optimization .

Yakuza: Like a Dragon Changed Everything And Nailed It On Day One

An Open-World RPG That Launched A New Era With The Confidence Of A Long-Time Franchise

  • Some minor performance issues on PC, but nothing major.

By 2020, Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio had ironed out the kinks in its open-world projects, and Yakuza had finally established itself as a reliable source of epic drama and silly nonsense. Then, the developer decided to change the protagonist, setting, and gameplay system, founding a new era not many die-hard fans asked for. On Day One, Yakuza: Like a Dragon needed to justify the switch to turn-based combat and the arrival of Ichiban.

The game didn't just make the pivot work, but it launched as one of the most confident RPGs of the modern era . The relentlessly optimistic Ichiban Kasuga wasn't Kiryu 2.0, and that was 100% the right decision. A low-level Yakuza fall man, Ichiban views the criminal underworld through the lens of Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy , transforming allies and enemies into JRPG archetypes. We didn't need a narrative explanation for the turn-based combat, but Yakuza: Like a Dragon provided one that helped make its new protagonist even more endearing .

Speaking of the combat, the battle system certainly took inspiration from the classics, but it added that Yakuza flair through its Job/class system and ridiculously over-the-top animations that juxtaposed perfectly with the "realistic" urban setting. Also, this massive 50+ hour open-world masterpiece launched with a completely optional management sim minigame that could have been a standalone release.

10 Best Open-World Games By Japanese Developers, Ranked

Nintendo, Capcom, Square Enix, and Sega have all published some of the best open-world games ever.

By Mark Sammut

Horizon Zero Dawn Looked And Played Like A Dream

A Technically Perfect Open-World RPG

  • The 2020 PC port had many technical issues, so I'm only talking about the PS4 version.

I went back and forth on whether to include Horizon Zero Dawn , since it toes the line between action-adventure and RPG. Ultimately, we are talking about a game with a traditional leveling system, weapon upgrades, skill trees, build specialization, elemental resistance, and a character-driven story. Sure, you experience Aloy's journey and not write your own, but narrative decisions aren't required for an RPG.

Debuting just a few days before The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , Horizon Zero Dawn managed to avoid being swallowed whole by Nintendo's juggernaut and the launch of the Switch, a feat only made possible thanks to the game's spotless launch cycle. During an era when every exciting new title comes with built-in scandals and compromises, HZD arrived with few significant bugs and visuals that seemed well beyond the PS4's capabilities .

As shown with Killzone ​​​​​​, Guerrilla Games loves its high-concept ideas, and a game about tribal hunters who use bows to fight hyper-advanced robot dinosaurs in a lush post-apocalyptic Earth would have devolved into B-grade schlock if handled poorly. However, from Day One, HZD was dead serious in execution, presentation, and gameplay . Except for the human combat, the gameplay was generally brilliant and satisfying, all the while avoiding bullet sponge enemies that feature in so many open-world RPGs.

Although slow to get going, the story absolutely sticks the landing thanks to a top-notch mystery that builds well throughout the long but not exhausting campaign. HZD wasn't BOTW , but it didn't need to be.

Guild Wars 2 Had As Perfect An MMO Launch As Possible

An Open-World RPG On Hard Mode

  • Servers were overwhelmed at first.

If open-world RPGs with perfect Day Ones are rare, then open-world MMORPGs with perfect Day Ones might as well be fictional . Even the genre's eternal ruler, World of Warcraft , had its share of issues at launch, despite hitting the ground running far quicker than nearly all of its subsequent competitors. The one exception is Guild Wars 2 , and ArenaNet specifically decided to do the exact opposite of WoW 's playbook.

By the standards of MMOs, GW2 's launch was unbelievably smooth . Admittedly, the servers were so overwhelmed with players that ArenaNet had to temporarily pause digital sales, but that is one of the best problems a game could have. GW2 solved the biggest issue of early MMOs – multi-hour queues – by revolutionizing Overflow Worlds so that players could load into temporary instances of the map and freely play, rather than wait for a spot on the server to open. Although updates would take the game to new heights, Guild Wars 2 1.0 was already near-perfect, and its no-subscription model was a breath of fresh air in 2012.

5 Open-World RPGs That Were Perfect From Day One
GTA 6 Is Treating Money the Way More Open-World Games Should
5 New Open-World RPGs That Are Officially 10/10
New Open-World Survival Game Is Fixing One of the Genre's Most Wasted Features

  • North Americans had to beg Nintendo to bring the game over.

OK, this one is a bit of a special case, and it has nothing to do with the game's actual quality. Famously, Nintendo didn't seem interested in releasing Xenoblade Chronicles in North America, prompting fans to stage the "Operation Rainfall" campaign to finally set things right. You could argue this nonsense disqualifies XC from a perfect launch, since millions of people didn't get to play it on Day One; however, the outcry was so loud because the game was so fantastic.

The Nintendo Wii was incredibly underpowered for its era, barely offering more juice than a GameCube. An expansive open-world RPG should not have worked on this console, but Monolith Soft not only succeeded in performing a technical miracle, but also a mechanical one . Besides somehow avoiding mid-zone loading screens in its major open areas, Xenoblade Chronicles tells an ambitious story set in a world found on the body of two warring titans, and you can actually see them in real-time.

Monolith introduced a real-time battle system that layered mechanics on top of each other, keeping it interesting for 50+ hours. The world and its enemies didn't feel static, and XC included quality-of-life adjustments that were ahead of the curve at the time. For an open-world RPG created on the Wii, XC was an uncompromised masterclass in scale and optimization .

Yakuza: Like a Dragon Changed Everything And Nailed It On Day One

An Open-World RPG That Launched A New Era With The Confidence Of A Long-Time Franchise

  • Some minor performance issues on PC, but nothing major.

By 2020, Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio had ironed out the kinks in its open-world projects, and Yakuza had finally established itself as a reliable source of epic drama and silly nonsense. Then, the developer decided to change the protagonist, setting, and gameplay system, founding a new era not many die-hard fans asked for. On Day One, Yakuza: Like a Dragon needed to justify the switch to turn-based combat and the arrival of Ichiban.

The game didn't just make the pivot work, but it launched as one of the most confident RPGs of the modern era . The relentlessly optimistic Ichiban Kasuga wasn't Kiryu 2.0, and that was 100% the right decision. A low-level Yakuza fall man, Ichiban views the criminal underworld through the lens of Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy , transforming allies and enemies into JRPG archetypes. We didn't need a narrative explanation for the turn-based combat, but Yakuza: Like a Dragon provided one that helped make its new protagonist even more endearing .

Speaking of the combat, the battle system certainly took inspiration from the classics, but it added that Yakuza flair through its Job/class system and ridiculously over-the-top animations that juxtaposed perfectly with the "realistic" urban setting. Also, this massive 50+ hour open-world masterpiece launched with a completely optional management sim minigame that could have been a standalone release.

10 Best Open-World Games By Japanese Developers, Ranked

Nintendo, Capcom, Square Enix, and Sega have all published some of the best open-world games ever.

By Mark Sammut

Horizon Zero Dawn Looked And Played Like A Dream

A Technically Perfect Open-World RPG

  • The 2020 PC port had many technical issues, so I'm only talking about the PS4 version.

I went back and forth on whether to include Horizon Zero Dawn , since it toes the line between action-adventure and RPG. Ultimately, we are talking about a game with a traditional leveling system, weapon upgrades, skill trees, build specialization, elemental resistance, and a character-driven story. Sure, you experience Aloy's journey and not write your own, but narrative decisions aren't required for an RPG.

Debuting just a few days before The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , Horizon Zero Dawn managed to avoid being swallowed whole by Nintendo's juggernaut and the launch of the Switch, a feat only made possible thanks to the game's spotless launch cycle. During an era when every exciting new title comes with built-in scandals and compromises, HZD arrived with few significant bugs and visuals that seemed well beyond the PS4's capabilities .

As shown with Killzone ​​​​​​, Guerrilla Games loves its high-concept ideas, and a game about tribal hunters who use bows to fight hyper-advanced robot dinosaurs in a lush post-apocalyptic Earth would have devolved into B-grade schlock if handled poorly. However, from Day One, HZD was dead serious in execution, presentation, and gameplay . Except for the human combat, the gameplay was generally brilliant and satisfying, all the while avoiding bullet sponge enemies that feature in so many open-world RPGs.

Although slow to get going, the story absolutely sticks the landing thanks to a top-notch mystery that builds well throughout the long but not exhausting campaign. HZD wasn't BOTW , but it didn't need to be.

Guild Wars 2 Had As Perfect An MMO Launch As Possible

An Open-World RPG On Hard Mode

  • Servers were overwhelmed at first.

If open-world RPGs with perfect Day Ones are rare, then open-world MMORPGs with perfect Day Ones might as well be fictional . Even the genre's eternal ruler, World of Warcraft , had its share of issues at launch, despite hitting the ground running far quicker than nearly all of its subsequent competitors. The one exception is Guild Wars 2 , and ArenaNet specifically decided to do the exact opposite of WoW 's playbook.

By the standards of MMOs, GW2 's launch was unbelievably smooth . Admittedly, the servers were so overwhelmed with players that ArenaNet had to temporarily pause digital sales, but that is one of the best problems a game could have. GW2 solved the biggest issue of early MMOs – multi-hour queues – by revolutionizing Overflow Worlds so that players could load into temporary instances of the map and freely play, rather than wait for a spot on the server to open. Although updates would take the game to new heights, Guild Wars 2 1.0 was already near-perfect, and its no-subscription model was a breath of fresh air in 2012.

5 Open-World RPGs That Were Perfect From Day One
GTA 6 Is Treating Money the Way More Open-World Games Should
5 New Open-World RPGs That Are Officially 10/10
New Open-World Survival Game Is Fixing One of the Genre's Most Wasted Features

item.title: Borderlands 4: Loveless Visual Paradox Nexus Build (One-Shot Sniper)
item.description:
Loveless is the sixth Vault Hunter in Borderlands 4, and a new VH means a new way to become OP! Loveless has many builds to pick from, but this Visual Paradox Nexus (VPN) build for Loveless in Borderlands 4 takes the cake by providing you with a one-shot build that capitalizes on Loveless' Sniper Rifles to one-shot every enemy and break into stealth to avoid damage, remain invisible, and ensure bosses are killed in seconds.

Borderlands 4: All Loveless Legendary Class Mods

Looking to improve your Loveless builds? You're going to need to know where to find all of her Legendary Class Mods (and know what they do)!

By Jake Fillery

Best Skills for the Loveless Visual Paradox Nexus Build

Hack / Slash Skill Tree (Blue)

Skill

Description

How it Works

Disdain (5/5)

Loveless gains increased Critical Hit Damage.

+25% Critical Hit Damage will help build your main damage source massively.

Odium (3/3)

Loveless' Melee Critical Hits receive increased benefit from Disdain.

Melee Critical Hits will now deal +500% Damage thanks to Disdain.

Ratio Technique (5/5)

Loveless gains Critical Hit Chance with Guns and Melee Attacks

Further +10% Gun Critical Hit Chance and +30% Melee Critical Hit Chance.

Stack Overflow (Augment)

Whenever Loveless enters Stealth, the Damage her next 3 Gun Shots deal is Stored. Loveless' next Function or Executable deals Stored Damage as Bonus Damage and consumes it.

Essential component of the build that means you shoot enemies, then use your Function for serious damage.

Death Begets Death (4/5)

Kill Skill. Loveless restores Action Skill Duration. Killing an enemy with Critical or Melee Damage gives double Action Skill Duration restoration.

Permanent uptime for the Action Skill, as each kill grants 8% more duration.

Methodical (5/5)

Loveless gains increased Gun Damage based on her Gun's Fire Rate. The lower the Fire Rate, the greater the bonus.

Gun Damage is increased up to +100% from Sniper Rifles with a low fire rate.

Retribution (5/5)

When a Clone dies, Loveless gains increased Gun and Critical Hit Damage for a Duration.

More buffs thanks to Clones (that you want dead), so you can get +40% Gun Damage+25% Critical Hit Damage.

Refactored Damage Formula (1/1)

Loveless' Sniper Rifle Damage is multiplied.

You need a Class Mod that has +1 in Refactored Damage Formula, as it DOUBLES Sniper damage instead of just +10%.

Killing Machine (1/3)

Kill Skill. Loveless fully restores her Function Cooldown and partially restores her Executable Cooldown.

Every kill restores your Function, which is your Kusarigama.

accelerat.exe (Capstone)

Activating VPN immediately spawns the maximum amount of Clones. While VPN is active, Loveless gains Executable to manifest an Acceleration Gate, which causes Gun Shots to have increased Damage and Projectile Speed.

The Acceleration Gate remains until Loveless has shot 3 times.

Any active Clones are absorbed when the Acceleration Gate is created, adding additional shots per Clone absorbed.

Use your Executable to increase Gun Damage by +250% and Projectile Speed by +50%.

Third Party (5/5)

Loveless gains increased Action Skill Damage and Status Effect Damage.

This bonus is increased for each active Clone or if Wyrm is active.

The more Clones, the more damage the Action Skill does. That's +50% per Clone!

The Sweet Science (5/5)

Footwork Skill. Moving generates Stacks of Footwork. Loveless gains Movement Speed for each Footwork Stack.

Footwork Stacks now provide Melee Damage. When at Max Stacks, enemies damaged by Loveless' Empowered Melee receive a random Status Effect.

Just moving around is going to increase Melee Damage.

Merry Bandwidth (3/3)

Loveless can have more active Clones.

+3 Clones, which buffs Third Party and accelerat.exe.

Flow State (3/3)

Dealing Melee Damage gives Loveless a Stack of Flow State for a Duration.

Stacks give Melee Damage.

Dealing Melee Damage rewards you with Stacks of Flow State, which give +33% Melee Damage with every Stack!

Manifestation Skill Tree (Red)

Skill

Description

How it Works

Corrupted Path (5/5)

Loveless gains increased Radiation Damage and Irradiation Chance.

Symbiosis Effect. Loveless always deals Bonus Radiation Damage. This effect scales with the amount of Symbiosis Stacks she currently has.

+25% Radiation Damage, which buffs the Kusarigama.

Overclock (5/5)

Loveless now deals increased Action Skill Damage and gains longer Action Skill Duration.

Action Skill now deals +40% Damage and lasts +25% longer to buff the Kusarigama

Critically Acclaimed (5/5)

Kill Skill. Critical Hit Kills by Loveless and Wyrm have a chance to refund Missing Action Skill Duration.

50% chance to extend Action Skill Duration with every Critical Hit Kill.

Neurokinetics (5/5)

When Loveless or Wyrm deal Critical Hit Damage, Loveless gains Increased Melee Damage for a duration.

Symbiosis Effect. When dealing Melee Damage, Loveless gains a chance to Heal herself for a portion of the damage she dealt. The portion she gets scales with her current amoutn of Symbiosis Stacks.

Critical Hits increase Kusarigama damage, and said damage dealt now heals you.

Perfect Execution (4/5)

loveless gains Critical Hit Chance on all Damage Dealt by Functions and Executables.

More Critical Hit Chance for Executables, which helps accelerat.exe

Best Equipment Loadout for Loveless Visual Paradox Nexus Build

Sniper Rifle: Wind Skimmer

Shoots 4 bullets at once for extremely high damage , but if you jump while shooting, it only consumes one bullet instead of four. You can also run it with Daedalus as the Licensed Part so that you can use SMG bullets and just have near-infinite Sniper shots!

Truck, Boomslang, Stealth & Seak, and the Solar Temper are all great choices. You need something that hits hard and fires slowly!

Repkit: Triple Bypass

Triple Bypass will be your essential Repkit. This comes with Heart Pump to try and help get your Action Skill back instantly if you lose it. The main thing to hunt for with Triple Bypass is Amp , as you can increase your Gun Damage by +200% after using it.

Ordnance: Jakobs Crit Throwing Knife

A Crit Throwing Knife is not essential, but it sure is nice. This will ensure you can throw it at a boss to gaurantee Critical Hit Damage against them to aid in your quest to insta-kill everything.

Class Mod: Montage Maker

You farm this from Vile Lictor, and you NEED a drop that has +1 in Refactored Damage Formula so it can double your Sniper Damage . The Class Mod itself is great, as killing an enemy with a Sniper Rifle has a 25% Chance to let you enter Stealth for 2 seconds, and Critical Hit Kills always trigger this effect, and in Stealth, you deal +50% Damage, so it's essentially: more damage and invisibility.

Shield: Watts 4 Dinner

It's a great shield for survivability, but really you just want something with Amp so that when your Energy Shields are full, you can gain an increase to Gun Damage.

Enhancement

This isn't really essential, but it's mainly about what you have. You want an Enhancement that increases Sniper Rifle Damage, and one that complements the gun manufacturer type you're using.

Firmware: High Caliber

High Caliber will increase Gun Damage and allow bullets to pierce enemies, which means they can go through additional enemies for more kills when mobbing.

Specializations

  • Groundbreaker
  • Now With Caffeine
  • I Am A Gun
  • A Honed Mind

Any spare points you have, give them to Brute for increased Gun Damage!

Loveless Sniper One-Shot Build Gameplay Loop

Whenever Loveless enters Stealth, the Damage her next 3 Gun Shots deal is Stored. The next Function or Executable deals the Stored Damage as Bonus Damage and consumes it. So essentially:

  1. Use your Action Skill.
  2. Fire three Sniper shots
  3. Use the Function to melee hit with your Kusarigama.
  4. Use your Melee Attack.
  5. Repeat.

item.title: First Diablo 5 Classes Officially Revealed
item.description:
Blizzard has officially revealed the first three Diablo 5 classes at BlizzCon. After the surprising announcement earlier in the day that the next Diablo game is coming in 2029, Blizzard continued the fun by confirming a few classes that players will be able to play as in the game.

Of all the announcements so far at BlizzCon, Diablo 5 being confirmed for 2029 is perhaps the most shocking. That launch window would see the game release just six years after Diablo 4 . While that may seem like a long time, for Diablo releases, it's incredibly quick. For context, there were 11 years between Diablo 3 and 4 . Even now, three years out, Blizzard has wasted no time detailing what players can expect from the upcoming sequel with the reveal of the first new Diablo 5 classes.

Diablo Netflix Show is Now Official

Blizzard confirms that Diablo is officially getting an animated Netflix TV show.

By Daniel Morris

First Three Diablo 5 Classes Revealed

During the Diablo 5: Forging the Next Era panel at BlizzCon 2026, the developer revealed the game's first three classes: Demon Hunter, Monk, and Plague Knight . It also promised "Diablo's largest class roster to date, with even more to come in the coming years. Given that the game is still at least three years out, it's of little surprise that Blizzard is still holding back some surprises for the future.

All Diablo 5 Classes

  • Demon Hunter : The Demon Hunter returns to stalk the forces of Hell with twin crossbows, striking from the shadows and leaping across the battlefield to annihilate their prey.
  • Monk : The Monk brings martial perfection back to Sanctuary, battering demons to a pulp with fists and calling down holy power to smite those who stand in their path.
  • Plague Knight : The all-new Plague Knight is the embodiment of walking death. They roam the battlefield, spreading disease and pestilence, ultimately consuming it for power.

Diablo veterans will immediately recognize the Demon Hunter and Monk from both Diablo 3 and Immortal . However, the Plague Knight is an entirely new Diablo class, with Blizzard giving players something fresh and exciting already, so far away from release. Given that players can expect the biggest class roster on launch, it's fair to say that even more familiar classes will be revealed when Blizzard is ready.

The Forging the Next Era panel also included some interesting details about how Diablo 5 will handle itemization. Blizzard claims that its "goal is to design items to feel readable, memorable, and worth chasing across hundreds of hours," inspired by Diablo 2 's design philosophy. Like that game, larger items take up more inventory slots, meaning inventory management becomes even more important than ever.

Brand-New Diablo 4 Class Officially Confirmed for 2027
First Diablo 5 Classes Officially Revealed
New Official Diablo 4 Release Confirmed for September 15
Diablo 5 Officially Announced

Blizzard does highlight that, right now, Diablo 5 is still in very early development, "and this reveal marks the beginning of an ongoing conversation with the Diablo player community." However, players will not have to wait long to find out more. Starting in 2027, the developer plans to "share regular updates offering a closer look at our progress, the ideas guiding development, and features taking shape along the way." In the meantime, Diablo 4 Seasons are expected to continue as normal while Blizzard works hard on the sequel.

Given that the game is still at least three years out, it's of little surprise that Blizzard is still holding back some surprises for the future.

All Diablo 5 Classes

  • Demon Hunter : The Demon Hunter returns to stalk the forces of Hell with twin crossbows, striking from the shadows and leaping across the battlefield to annihilate their prey.
  • Monk : The Monk brings martial perfection back to Sanctuary, battering demons to a pulp with fists and calling down holy power to smite those who stand in their path.
  • Plague Knight : The all-new Plague Knight is the embodiment of walking death. They roam the battlefield, spreading disease and pestilence, ultimately consuming it for power.

Diablo veterans will immediately recognize the Demon Hunter and Monk from both Diablo 3 and Immortal . However, the Plague Knight is an entirely new Diablo class, with Blizzard giving players something fresh and exciting already, so far away from release. Given that players can expect the biggest class roster on launch, it's fair to say that even more familiar classes will be revealed when Blizzard is ready.

The Forging the Next Era panel also included some interesting details about how Diablo 5 will handle itemization. Blizzard claims that its "goal is to design items to feel readable, memorable, and worth chasing across hundreds of hours," inspired by Diablo 2 's design philosophy. Like that game, larger items take up more inventory slots, meaning inventory management becomes even more important than ever.

Blizzard does highlight that, right now, Diablo 5 is still in very early development, "and this reveal marks the beginning of an ongoing conversation with the Diablo player community." However, players will not have to wait long to find out more. Starting in 2027, the developer plans to "share regular updates offering a closer look at our progress, the ideas guiding development, and features taking shape along the way." In the meantime, Diablo 4 Seasons are expected to continue as normal while Blizzard works hard on the sequel.

item.title: After 4 Years, Hearthstone Is Finally Adding a Brand-New Class
item.description:
Hearthstone is finally getting a new playable class in the form of Monk. Announced during BlizzCon 2026, Monk will mark Hearthstone 's 12th class to date.

Blizzard's hit collectible card game launched with nine classes in 2014, then added Demon Hunter six years later. Hearthstone 's most recent class addition was Death Knight, launched in late 2022. Both have meaningfully expanded the game's meta, with Monk being expected to follow suit.

Hearthstone: 8 Most Overpowered Cards Of All Time, Ranked

These Hearthstone cards have powers that are nothing short of game-breaking.

By Ollie Tuscarny

Hearthstone's Monk Class Is Coming in Early 2027

Blizzard plans to release Monk in March 2027, though it has yet to announce an exact launch date. The developer is also keeping most gameplay details under wraps, saying only that the class will bring its signature "fluid playstyle and adaptable nature" to the CCG. The reveal cinematic that premiered during BlizzCon 2026 stars legendary Pandaren "brewmaster" Chen Stormstout, who will presumably be the default hero of the new Hearthstone class. Monk's Hero Power, cards, and any unique mechanics have yet to be revealed.

Blizzard Teased Hearthstone's Monk Class Years Ago

The newly announced arrival may not surprise the most attentive CCG fans, as Blizzard has been dropping hints of Hearthstone 's Monk class for years, both intentionally and less so. As far back as January 2022, dataminers discovered a special Xuen hero greeting intended for matches against a Monk, fueling speculation that the class was already somewhere on the content roadmap. Blizzard actively stirred those theories again in October 2024 with an expansion teaser featuring content creators dressed in robes reminiscent of the Monk attire, although the campaign ultimately led to The Great Dark Beyond expansion rather than a new class. Another particularly conspicuous clue surfaced in February 2026, when players spotted an apparent Monk Coin in the game's PC client.

Monk Will Bring Hearthstone to the Brink of Playable Class Parity with World of Warcraft

Monk will bring Hearthstone one step closer to matching the playable class lineup of World of Warcraft , which currently includes 13 classes. After March 2027, Evoker will be the only WoW class without a direct playable counterpart in the popular CCG. That does not necessarily mean it will follow anytime soon. Monk itself will have taken nearly 15 years to make the jump from WoW to Hearthstone , or about 13 years when measured from Hearthstone 's release date.

After 4 Years, Hearthstone Is Finally Adding a Brand-New Class
New Official $975 Warcraft Release Confirmed for 2027
New Official $400 Warcraft Release Confirmed for 2027
Hearthstone Is Retiring Another Game Mode

How exactly Blizzard will translate Monk into Hearthstone remains to be seen. The developer's previous class additions introduced new defining systems: Demon Hunter debuted with Outcast and a one-mana Hero Power, while Death Knight brought Corpses and Rune-based deck building. Hearthstone already has an extensive range of class-specific mechanics and keywords, giving Blizzard plenty of room to make Monk distinct without simply recreating its World of Warcraft abilities, but while still staying true to them.

New Hearthstone Expansion Coming October 20

While awaiting more details about Monk, Hearthstone players can look forward to the CCG's 34th expansion. Titled Reign of the Black Empire , the content drop launches on October 20 and takes the game back to ancient Azeroth. It introduces a new keyword, Assemble, which combines two compatible cards into a more powerful creation, seemingly making it a natural fit for decks built around value trading.
